title: Strict Roos cone comparison with total derived inverse limit and evaluations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact. Write $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ for the category of strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system]. Let $X_\bullet$ be any integer cochain complex of strict towers, with transitions $t_n:X_{n+1}\to X_n$, and let $u:X_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ be a K-injective resolution in $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex $I_\bullet$ such that every chain map from an acyclic complex of towers to $I_\bullet$ is chain homotopic to zero. Derived categories and quasi-isomorphisms are as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set $P_X=\prod_n X_n$ termwise and $s_X:P_X\to P_X$ by $\mathrm{pr}_n s_X=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism], and put $\operatorname{Roos}(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$ with differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-d y-(1-s_X)x,d x)$. Define $\operatorname{Roos}(I)$ in the same way, and $L_I=\lim_n I_n$ termwise, which represents the total right derived inverse limit of $X_\bullet$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Both arrows in the zigzag
$$\operatorname{Roos}(X)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Roos}(u)}\operatorname{Roos}(I)\xleftarrow{\eta}L_I$$
are quasi-isomorphisms, where $\operatorname{Roos}(u)$ applies $\prod_nu_n$ to both cone coordinates and $\eta(z)=(0,z)$. For each $n$, the resulting isomorphism $\theta:\operatorname{Roos}(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim X_\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ is compatible with evaluation: $e_n\theta$ equals the chain projection $\operatorname{Roos}(X)\to X_n$, $(y,x)\mapsto\mathrm{pr}_n x$, in $D(\mathcal A)$, where $e_n:R\lim X_\bullet\to X_n$ is represented by $L_I\to I_n$ followed by $u_n^{-1}$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products, and Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit. The evaluation-preserving zigzag for an arbitrary strict tower is the agent-written comparison with the K-injective Roos model, as needed by the last paragraph of def-weil-rationalization-karoubi.

proof.text: Write $C(T)=\operatorname{Roos}(T)$. Apply [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] to the given small ringed site: its exact-countable-product hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis of this item. The coordinate order here is (shifted target product, source product); the cone-and-shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $d(y,x)=(-dy-(1-s_T)x,dx)$ in this order, so its $\mathsf C$ is this $C$. The identity $u_nt_n=t_n^Iu_{n+1}$ gives $P(u)s_X=s_IP(u)$ after each projection. Consequently $(y,x)\mapsto(P(u)y,P(u)x)$ commutes with the displayed differential and is exactly $C(u)$. Evaluation is exact by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so $u$ is the quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes to which the descent-to-$D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$ clause of the comparison lemma applies. A functor sends an invertible morphism to an invertible morphism; thus $C(u)$ is invertible in $D(\mathcal A)$. Applying cohomology shows that the chain map $C(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products; Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; strict-cone functor supplied by the cited existing comparison lemma.

proof.text: The index category $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is small, so [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck] makes $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ Grothendieck abelian. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] in that category to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $v:I_\bullet\to J_\bullet$, where $J_\bullet$ is K-injective and every $J^r_\bullet$ is an injective tower object. Both $I_\bullet$ and $J_\bullet$ are K-injective; hence [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] says that $v$ is a homotopy equivalence in the category of tower complexes. Its inverse and its homotopies are tower maps, not merely unrelated maps at the individual levels. We use this replacement only to invoke the injective-term normalization of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]: applied to $v$ as a resolution of $I_\bullet$, it states that $\eta_J:L_J=\lim J_n\to C(J)$, $z\mapsto(0,z)$, is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck; derived.tex Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, injective-term computation.

proof.text:
Termwise limit sends a tower chain homotopy $h$ to the chain homotopy $\lim h$: for each degree its components preserve compatible sequences, and applying this additive functor to $f-g=dh+hd$ gives the same equation on limits. Thus the homotopy inverse of $v$ from Step 2 gives a homotopy inverse of $L(v):L_I\to L_J$, making $L(v)$ a quasi-isomorphism. The functor clause of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] also makes $C(v)$ a quasi-isomorphism, as in Step 1. The formula $\eta_I(z)=(0,z)$ is a chain map because $(1-s_I)z=0$. On the two coordinates one has the equality of chain maps
$$C(v)\eta_I=\eta_JL(v).$$
After cohomology, the three maps $C(v)$, $\eta_J$, and $L(v)$ are isomorphisms; therefore so is $H^r(\eta_I)=H^r(C(v))^{-1}H^r(\eta_J)H^r(L(v))$ for every $r$. This proves that the specified inclusion $\eta_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism even when $I$ does not have injective terms.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; explicit homotopy-equivalence and coordinate-square extension of sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], the given K-injective resolution computes the total right derived limit by $L_I$. Define $\theta=\eta_I^{-1}C(u):C(X)\to L_I$ in $D(\mathcal A)$; Steps 1 and 3 make it an isomorphism. Let $a_n^T:C(T)\to T_n$ be $(y,x)\mapsto\mathrm{pr}_nx$, and let $p_n:L_I\to I_n$ be the limit projection. These are chain maps: the second coordinate of the Roos differential is $dx$. Their formulas give
$$a_n^I\eta_I=p_n,\qquad a_n^IC(u)=u_na_n^X.$$
Hence $p_n\theta=a_n^IC(u)=u_na_n^X$ in the derived category. Exact evaluation from [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] makes $u_n$ a quasi-isomorphism, so $e_n=u_n^{-1}p_n$ is the evaluation specified in the statement, and $e_n\theta=a_n^X$. This is the required compatibility for each $n$, for the actual displayed zigzag rather than an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism of Roos triangles.
